title: Spec before code
subtitle: Acceptance criteria and "out of scope" shrink the agent’s diff
mission: The Pão de Mel order app got serious: three shops now, and a real team. Duda (product analyst) writes the issues, Bia (tech lead) hands them to the coding agent and reviews the PR. Next feature: scheduling pickups. Compare three specs of the same feature and see what the agent does with each one.

why.simples:
Ask a bakery for "a birthday cake" and you get three tiers, candles, frosting and a name on top. You wanted a simple cake for 10 people.
Whoever gets a vague order doesn’t do less: they do what they imagine you want. Writing down first what "done" means (and what’s out) saves you the wrong cake.
why.dev:
A good issue for an agent has: the goal in one sentence, verifiable acceptance criteria (numbers, limits, messages), what’s out of scope and how to verify (test command). Each criterion becomes a test; "out of scope" cuts the inventions.
Before letting the agent edit, ask for a plan: in Claude Code, `claude --permission-mode plan` (or Shift+Tab until "plan mode on" shows) makes it read and propose without touching disk; in Cursor, Plan Mode also opens with Shift+Tab. On GitHub you can assign the issue to Copilot: the issue text is the spec it gets.
why.especialista:
A plan is a cheap spec written "backwards": the agent shows what it understood, and fixing a paragraph takes minutes, while fixing 640 lines takes hours and review rounds. That’s why the vague request with a plan already lands close to the partial one.
In teams it pays to have an issue template with fixed sections (Goal, Acceptance criteria, Out of scope, How to verify) and an automatic checker that complains about issues without criteria before they reach the agent. This lesson’s numbers come from a made-up scenario, but the direction (open scope → bigger diff → more review) is what teams report.

planQs.vague: What times does the shop take? Is there a per-hour limit? Should the customer get an SMS? Who changes bookings?
planQs.partial: How many days ahead can people book? Does the time show on the receipt?
planQs.full: No questions: the plan lists one test per criterion and doesn’t touch SMS, payment or admin.

data.gradeSystem: You grade task specs for a coding agent. Read the spec and reply with JSON only: {"criteria": number of verifiable acceptance criteria (with numbers or observable results), "out_of_scope": true if it says what is out of scope, "question": the most important question you would ask before coding}.

steps:
Create docs/specs/schedule-pickup.md in your project (swap the feature for yours):
# Schedule pickup
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Customer picks a day and time between 7am and 7pm
- [ ] At most 20 pickups per hour
- [ ] Booking up to 2 days ahead
- [ ] The receipt shows the time
## Out of scope
- SMS, payment, admin screen
## How to verify
- npm test

Ask for a plan before any edit. In Claude Code:
claude --permission-mode plan
Then type: Read docs/specs/schedule-pickup.md and propose a plan with the files you will change and one test per criterion. Nothing out of scope.
In Cursor, use Plan Mode (Shift+Tab in the Agent input). In Copilot, ask for the plan in chat before switching to agent mode.

Check the plan against the list: does each criterion have a test? Does any item mention SMS, payment or admin? Fix the plan, approve it and, at the end, run:
git diff --stat
recipe.ok: the plan has one test per criterion and doesn’t mention SMS, payment or admin, and git diff --stat lists only the files that were in the plan.
